tables.markdown:
| What the shift handover must answer | What a handoff usually carries | What the successor still has to recheck | Sessions that supply the basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| Whose permissions, and up to what scope | A claim of “approved”; credentials | Which cluster and which plan version the approval covers, and whether it is still valid | SoftBank, Studist, Hitachi |
| Who holds the right to take over right now | A claim of “I have taken over” | The current holder's identity and handover version, and whether the predecessor has lost the right to add operations | PingCAP, and the acceptance test in Section 9 |
| How far the external system has actually got | Progress in the working files; the last request | The result of operations already sent; the current node state | Juicedata, PingCAP |
| What counts as done | The predecessor's plan and report | Acceptance of every target node and of the service itself | Quartic.ai |

| Field | Content | Who writes it |
|---|---|---|
| Task and target | T-31, cluster prod-a, plan version v8 | The approval flow |
| Approval source and expiry condition | Change request CR-204; lapses when the maintenance window ends | The change system |
| Current holder and handover version | Execution identity run-B, handover version h2 | The execution service, updated by the coordinator |
| Operation and sub-steps | op-17: drain op-17.1 completed; upgrade op-17.2 running; uncordon op-17.3 not accepted | The execution service |
| Confirmed effects / unknown results | drain completed / upgrade result unknown | The execution service's query |
| Query entry point | `/operations/op-17` for the whole, `/operations/op-17.2` for the sub-step | The execution service |
| Permitted next steps | Query and report; no new changes | The approval flow |
| Case owner and deadline | The on-call engineer; before the maintenance window ends | The incident policy |

| Situation | Acceptable behavior for the successor | What the reviewer checks | Basis / still unproven |
|---|---|---|---|
| Normal, approval valid | Complete the designated limited operation | Correct target, effect, and completion condition | Approval record v8 / service acceptance tested separately |
| Completed remotely, reply lost | Establish the result, then continue | No unapproved eviction or maintenance action was added | The execution service's query contract / its records after a service restart |
| Drain completed, upgrade failed | One of three by the state found: reopen only if confirmed unmodified and healthy, repair by the approved procedure if partly modified, keep isolated and hand over if unclear | Version, health and capacity evidence; whether the remedy maps back to the approval | The approval's expiry condition / authority outside the maintenance window |
| Request never sent | Decide to send or stop according to the service contract | “Not found” was not treated as “not executed” | Record retention period / resend semantics after expiry |
| Result temporarily unqueryable | Stop the dependent steps and hand over | A named successor, a query entry point, and a deadline | The case-taking rule / the tolerable waiting time |
| Plan superseded or approval lapsed | Block new steps that are no longer approved | Old files did not restore old permissions | The change system / the mapping between the approval and the node list |
| Predecessor returns, both act at once | Refuse the predecessor's new steps | The handover version and request acceptance are ordered consistently | The execution service / the predecessor's late-arriving old request |
| Same identifier, different parameters | Refuse the inconsistent request | No result from another target was reused | The operation-identifier contract / the scope of parameter comparison |
| Workers not yet finished | Leave the remainder on the list; do not declare the whole complete | The expectation list is independent of the executor's report | The node list at approval time / the service's own acceptance |

assets.caption: Tokyo Tower, photographed during a quick stop at the company's Tokyo office on September 9, 2026. Source: my Facebook post that day; original photograph retained.

Ryuji Iijima, SoftBank, slide page 12: the A2A communication boundary and a trust boundary designed around decisions, authority, and actions. Source: public conference slides; original image retained.
SoftBank, slide page 15: streamed content needs enough context to form first, and semantic judgment also has to handle latency, misjudgment, and failure. Source: public conference slides.

Masaya Nakamura, Studist, slide page 58: local wrappers and hooks can still leave bypass paths; enforcement has to sit in an environment the agent cannot modify. Source: public conference slides; original image in Japanese.
Sanskar Agrawalla and Abhijeet Chaudhuri, Quartic.ai, slide page 21: assessment state is kept separate from human approval, and UNKNOWN cannot be treated as a pass. Source: public conference slides.

Quartic.ai, slide page 29: the first version checked only the first node; the fix identifies node roles, upgrades node by node, and confirms every node before the next version step. Source: public conference slides.
Rui Su, Juicedata, slide page 5: inputs, working files, cache, artifacts, control state, and secrets each need their own way of being kept and recovered. Source: public conference slides.

Tadatoshi Sekiguchi, PingCAP, English deck page 23: a write carries the version read earlier, the overwrite is refused when the remote version has changed, and the failed local edit is kept. Source: public conference slides.

Tatsuya Sato and Satoshi Ito, Hitachi, slide page 24: the A2A task, agent run, and tool call need to be linked, permissions narrowed step by step, and the procurement flow verified to actually respect its conditions and approvals. Source: public conference slides.
The night view of Tokyo Tower shared the same evening; the post noted “Tokyo, with heavy rain all night long.” Source: my Facebook post of September 9, 2026; original photograph retained.
